sources.title: A Computational Introduction to Number Theory and Algebra (Version 2.1)
sources.notes: Victor Shoup. The version history on PDF page 3 dates Version 2.1 to January 21, 2008. Locators refer to this version’s printed pages. Sections 3.2–3.3 explicitly charge for long-integer digits and reject unit-cost unbounded arithmetic.

sources.title: Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach (author-hosted draft)
sources.notes: Sanjeev Arora and Boaz Barak. Locators use the numbered pages and theorem numbers in the January 2007 author draft, not the later book edition.

theorems.name: InclusionBench.Support.polynomialSuccinctIntegerArray_intro
theorems.statement:
∀ {array : InclusionBench.Word → InclusionBench.Support.SuccinctIntegerArray},
  (InclusionBench.Support.PolynomialNatural fun input => (array input).length) →
    (InclusionBench.Support.PolynomialIntegerEntry fun input index => (array input).entry index) →
      InclusionBench.Support.PolynomialSuccinctIntegerArray array
theorems.locator: Kernel-proved in InclusionSupport.SuccinctIntegerArrays from the exact definitions and previously registered bridges. Background: Shoup §§3.2–3.3, printed pp.52–62 (bit cost and signed representation); Arora–Barak §1.2.2, Claims 1.8–1.9, printed pp.19–21 (finite-alphabet/tape simulations), and Theorem 2.8(1), printed p.44 (polynomial composition). No new literature premise is imported.
theorems.model_alignment: Kernel-proved wrapper over the existing IntegerArrays and Closure library; this module introduces no axiom. A single binary-length machine and a single entry machine work uniformly for every original input and binary index. PolynomialSuccinctIntegerArray does not assert polynomial numeric length, full-array output, or efficient sums over the represented range.

theorems.name: InclusionBench.Support.polynomialSuccinctIntegerArray_length_bits
theorems.statement:
∀ {array : InclusionBench.Word → InclusionBench.Support.SuccinctIntegerArray},
  InclusionBench.Support.PolynomialSuccinctIntegerArray array →
    ∃ bound,
      ∀ (input : InclusionBench.Word),
        InclusionBench.Support.integerBitSize ↑(array input).length ≤
          InclusionBench.Counting.polynomialValue bound (List.length input)
theorems.locator: Kernel-proved in InclusionSupport.SuccinctIntegerArrays from the exact definitions and previously registered bridges. Background: Shoup §§3.2–3.3, printed pp.52–62 (bit cost and signed representation); Arora–Barak §1.2.2, Claims 1.8–1.9, printed pp.19–21 (finite-alphabet/tape simulations), and Theorem 2.8(1), printed p.44 (polynomial composition). No new literature premise is imported.
theorems.model_alignment: Kernel-proved wrapper over the existing IntegerArrays and Closure library; this module introduces no axiom. A single binary-length machine and a single entry machine work uniformly for every original input and binary index. PolynomialSuccinctIntegerArray does not assert polynomial numeric length, full-array output, or efficient sums over the represented range. The entry bound charges exactly 2*(input.length + integerBitSize(index:Int))+3 bits for the fixed pair encoding, including its sign bit. The length bound controls its binary representation only; exponentially large cardinalities remain possible.

theorems.name: InclusionBench.Support.polynomialIntegerEntry_bit_bound
theorems.statement:
∀ {entry : InclusionBench.Word → Nat → Int},
  InclusionBench.Support.PolynomialIntegerEntry entry →
    ∃ bound,
      ∀ (input : InclusionBench.Word) (index : Nat),
        InclusionBench.Support.integerBitSize (entry input index) ≤
          InclusionBench.Counting.polynomialValue bound
            (2 * (List.length input + InclusionBench.Support.integerBitSize ↑index) + 3)

theorems.name: InclusionBench.Support.fp_succinctIntegerArray_read
theorems.statement:
∀ {array : InclusionBench.Word → InclusionBench.Support.SuccinctIntegerArray} {index : InclusionBench.Word → Nat},
  InclusionBench.Support.PolynomialSuccinctIntegerArray array →
    InclusionBench.Support.PolynomialNatural index →
      (∀ (input : InclusionBench.Word), index input < (array input).length) →
        InclusionBench.Transducers.FP fun input =>
          InclusionBench.Support.succinctIntegerArrayRead (array input) (index input)
theorems.locator: Kernel-proved in InclusionSupport.SuccinctIntegerArrays from the exact definitions and previously registered bridges. Background: Shoup §§3.2–3.3, printed pp.52–62 (bit cost and signed representation); Arora–Barak §1.2.2, Claims 1.8–1.9, printed pp.19–21 (finite-alphabet/tape simulations), and Theorem 2.8(1), printed p.44 (polynomial composition). No new literature premise is imported.
theorems.model_alignment: Kernel-proved wrapper over the existing IntegerArrays and Closure library; this module introduces no axiom. A single binary-length machine and a single entry machine work uniformly for every original input and binary index. PolynomialSuccinctIntegerArray does not assert polynomial numeric length, full-array output, or efficient sums over the represented range. The index must itself be uniformly binary-computable, and the explicit inside premise proves each requested index is below the represented length. The pure read operation returns zero outside the range, but this computational wrapper only claims the in-range case.

            InclusionBench.Support.succinctIntegerArrayZip operation (first input) (second input)

theorems.name: InclusionBench.Support.polynomialSuccinctIntegerArray_materialize
theorems.statement:
∀ {array : InclusionBench.Word → InclusionBench.Support.SuccinctIntegerArray},
  InclusionBench.Support.PolynomialSuccinctIntegerArray array →
    ∀ (bound : List Nat),
      (∀ (input : InclusionBench.Word),
          (array input).length ≤ InclusionBench.Counting.polynomialValue bound (List.length input)) →
        InclusionBench.Support.PolynomialIntegerArray fun input =>
          InclusionBench.Support.materializeSuccinctIntegerArray (array input)
theorems.locator: Kernel-proved in InclusionSupport.SuccinctIntegerArrays from the exact definitions and previously registered bridges. Background: Shoup §§3.2–3.3, printed pp.52–62 (bit cost and signed representation); Arora–Barak §1.2.2, Claims 1.8–1.9, printed pp.19–21 (finite-alphabet/tape simulations), and Theorem 2.8(1), printed p.44 (polynomial composition). No new literature premise is imported.
theorems.model_alignment: Kernel-proved wrapper over the existing IntegerArrays and Closure library; this module introduces no axiom. A single binary-length machine and a single entry machine work uniformly for every original input and binary index. PolynomialSuccinctIntegerArray does not assert polynomial numeric length, full-array output, or efficient sums over the represented range. Materialization enumerates List.range(length) and requires an explicit polynomial bound on the NUMERIC count. For a uniformly accessible family, the materialize_iff theorem proves this bound is necessary as well as sufficient; bit-length bounds alone do not permit exponential output.
